title: Hand-rolled argv parsing to Boost.Program_options
summary: An argument loop built on strcmp and atoi becomes an options_description and a variables_map. Required options are checked in notify, so --help is looked at first.

turns.user: arg parsing in main is strcmp hell. boost is already a dep, move it to program_options. want --help too

assistant.body: Got it! The hand-written loop becomes Boost.Program_options. The accepted options are listed in an options_description, store puts the result of parse_command_line into a variables_map, and notify writes the values back into host and port. Unlike atoi, a value like --port abc no longer turns silently into 0. It throws a po::error, and so does an unknown option. Printing desc gives the usage text for free, so all that strcmp boilerplate goes away.

turns.user: oh, port should be required with no default. prod once came up on 8080 by accident

assistant.body: Swap default_value for required. Note: help is checked before notify, and that matters here. The required check happens inside notify, so --help alone still prints the usage and exits without a port. Only a missing port gets the error naming the option, followed by the usage.
